title: List Environments
text: List environments environments list-like properties. implemented listenv package. main features list environment summarized table: example,
code: > x <- listenv(a = 1, b = 2, c = "hello") > x A ‘listenv’ vector with 3 elements (‘a’, ‘b’, ‘c’). > length(x) [1] 3 > names(x) [1] "a" "b" "c" > x$a [1] 1 > x[[3]] <- toupper(x[[3]]) > x$c [1] "HELLO" > y <- x > y$d <- y$a + y[["b"]] > names(y)[2] <- "a" > y$a [1] 1 > y A ‘listenv’ vector with 4 elements (‘a’, ‘a’, ‘c’, ‘d’). > identical(y, x) [1] TRUE > for (ii in seq_along(x)) { +     cat(sprintf("Element %d (%s): %s\n", ii, sQuote(names(x)[ii]),  +         x[[ii]])) + } Element 1 (‘a’): 1 Element 2 (‘a’): 2 Element 3 (‘c’): HELLO Element 4 (‘d’): 3 > x[c(1, 3)] <- list(2, "Hello world!") > x A ‘listenv’ vector with 4 elements (‘a’, ‘a’, ‘c’, ‘d’). > y <- as.list(x) > str(y) List of 4  $ a: num 2  $ a: num 2  $ c: chr "Hello world!"  $ d: num 3 > z <- as.listenv(y) > z A ‘listenv’ vector with 4 elements (‘a’, ‘a’, ‘c’, ‘d’). > identical(z, x) [1] FALSE > all.equal(z, x) [1] TRUE

text: Analogously lists, contrary plain environments, list environments can dimensions corresponding names. example, easy way quickly get overview coerce list, e.g. Individual elements list environment can accessed using standard subsetting syntax, e.g. can assign individual elements similarly, e.g. can also assign multiple elements dimensional subsetting, e.g. Concurrently dimensional names possible names individual elements just list environments without dimensions. example, Contrary lists, element names preserved also multi-dimensional subsetting, e.g. Note, whenever dimensions set using dim(x) <- dims dimensional names element names removed, e.g. behavior design, cf. help("dim", package="base"). allocate “empty” list environment array (NULL:s) given dimension, Rows columns can dropped assigning NULL, e.g. drop first third column list-environment matrix, :
code: > x <- as.listenv(1:6) > dim(x) <- c(2, 3) > dimnames(x) <- list(c("a", "b"), c("A", "B", "C")) > x A ‘listenv’ matrix with 6 elements (unnamed) arranged in 2x3 rows (‘a’, ‘b’) and columns (‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’). > as.list(x)   A B C a 1 3 5 b 2 4 6 > x[["a", "B"]] [1] 3 > x[[1, 2]] [1] 3 > x[[1, "B"]] [1] 3 > x[["b", "B"]] <- -x[["b", "B"]] > as.list(x)   A B  C a 1 3  5 b 2 -4 6 > x[2, -1] <- 98:99 > as.list(x)   A B  C  a 1 3  5  b 2 98 99 > x["a", c(1, 3)] <- list(97, "foo") > as.list(x)   A  B  C     a 97 3  "foo" b 2  98 99    > x[] <- 1:6 > as.list(x)   A B C a 1 3 5 b 2 4 6 > names(x) <- letters[seq_along(x)] > x A ‘listenv’ matrix with 6 elements (‘a’, ‘b’, ‘c’, ..., ‘f’) arranged in 2x3 rows (‘a’, ‘b’) and columns (‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’). > x[["a"]] [1] 1 > x[["f"]] [1] 6 > x[c("a", "f")] A ‘listenv’ vector with 2 elements (‘a’, ‘f’). > unlist(x) a b c d e f  1 2 3 4 5 6  > as.list(x)   A B C a 1 3 5 b 2 4 6 attr(,"names") [1] "a" "b" "c" "d" "e" "f" > x[1, 2] A ‘listenv’ vector with 1 element (‘c’). > x[1, 2, drop = FALSE] A ‘listenv’ matrix with 1 element (‘c’) arranged in 1x1 rows (‘a’) and columns (‘B’). > x[1:2, 2:1] A ‘listenv’ matrix with 4 elements (‘c’, ‘d’, ‘a’, ‘b’) arranged in 2x2 rows (‘a’, ‘b’) and columns (‘B’, ‘A’). > x[2, ] A ‘listenv’ vector with 3 elements (‘b’, ‘d’, ‘f’). > x[2, , drop = FALSE] A ‘listenv’ matrix with 3 elements (‘b’, ‘d’, ‘f’) arranged in 1x3 rows (‘b’) and columns (‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’). > x["b", -2, drop = FALSE] A ‘listenv’ matrix with 2 elements (‘b’, ‘f’) arranged in 1x2 rows (‘b’) and columns (‘A’, ‘C’). > dim(x) <- NULL > names(x) NULL > x <- listenv() > dim(x) <- c(2, 3) > dimnames(x) <- list(c("a", "b"), c("A", "B", "C")) > x A ‘listenv’ matrix with 6 elements (unnamed) arranged in 2x3 rows (‘a’, ‘b’) and columns (‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’). > x[, c(1, 3)] <- NULL > x A ‘listenv’ matrix with 2 elements (unnamed) arranged in 2x1 rows (‘a’, ‘b’) and columns (‘B’).

title: List Environments
text: List environments name suggests environments. Whenever working environments R, important understand environments mutable whereas basic data types R immutable. example, consider following function assigns zero element object x: pass regular list function, see x unaffected assignment. lists immutable R. However, pass environment instead, find x affected assignment. environments mutable R. Since list environments inherits environments, also goes , e.g. also important understand just content environment mutable also attributes. example, importantly, since dimensions names also attributes, also means mutable. example, Copyright Henrik Bengtsson, 2015-2018
code: > setA <- function(x) { +     x$a <- 0 +     x + } > x <- list(a = 1) > y <- setA(x) > x$a [1] 1 > y$a [1] 0 > x <- new.env() > x$a <- 1 > y <- setA(x) > x$a [1] 0 > y$a [1] 0 > x <- listenv(a = 1) > y <- setA(x) > x$a [1] 0 > y$a [1] 0 > x <- listenv(a = 1) > y <- x > attr(y, "foo") <- "Hello!" > attr(x, "foo") [1] "Hello!" > x <- as.listenv(1:6) > dim(x) <- c(2, 3) > x A ‘listenv’ matrix with 6 elements (unnamed) arranged in 2x3 unnamed rows and columns. > y <- x > dim(y) <- c(3, 2) > x A ‘listenv’ matrix with 6 elements (unnamed) arranged in 3x2 unnamed rows and columns.

title: Version 0.7.0
text: Now possible set dimension empty list environment without first resizing length(), e.g. x <- listenv(); dim(x) <- c(2, 3). Now possible remove multiple elements assigning NULL, e.g. x[c(2:3, 10)] <- NULL x[, "B"] <- NULL. Added lengths() list environments. Requires R (>= 3.3.0). dim_na(x) <- dims, dims contain exactly one missing value, set “missing” dimension based length x dimensions specified, e.g. length(x) == 6, dim_na(x) <- c(2, NA) set dim(x) <- c(2, 3). works types object dimensions can assigned - list environments. Added .matrix(), .array(), .vector(), .matrix() list environments.

title: Version 0.7.0
text: print() named, empty list environment output empty string. Removing element list environment remove dimensions, e.g. x$<- NULL.

title: Version 0.7.0
text: Function map() renamed mapping() corresponding replacement function. map() map<-() functions soon deprecated eventually defunct. x <- listenv(length = n) defunct; use x <- listenv(); length(x) <- n instead.

title: Version 0.4.0
text: Added .listenv(). CONSISTENCY: Assigning NULL now removes element just lists, e.g. x$<- NULL. assign value NULL, x[''] <-  list(NULL). Added support subsetting [(), returns another list environment, e.g. x[2:3], x[-1], x[c(TRUE, FALSE)]. Added [<- assignment, e.g. x[''] <- 1 x[2:3] <- c(3,8). CLEANUP: Dropped stray debug code.
